title: Symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAD)
question: What antithrombotic and procedural management fits stroke or TIA from 50–99% intracranial stenosis?
population: Stroke or TIA attributed to 50–99% stenosis of a major intracranial artery
Rule 3 also covers ipsilateral >30% stenosis within 24 h of minor stroke/high-risk TIA

rules.recommendation: Add clopidogrel 75 mg/day to aspirin for up to 90 days

rules.condition: Minor stroke or high-risk TIA within 24 h with ipsilateral >30% stenosis of a major intracranial artery (applies below this entry's 50–99% range; not the THALES ≥50% TIA criterion)
rules.recommendation: Ticagrelor 90 mg BID added to aspirin for up to 30 days might be considered

rules.condition: Presumed atherosclerotic minor stroke/TIA at 24–72 h

rules.recommendation: Cilostazol 200 mg/day added to aspirin or clopidogrel might be considered

rules.condition: Considering clopidogrel alone, aspirin/dipyridamole, ticagrelor alone or cilostazol alone

rules.recommendation: SBP <140 mm Hg, high-intensity statin, at least moderate physical activity

rules.condition: Severe 70–99% stenosis as initial treatment, even if on an antithrombotic at the time

rules.recommendation: Do not angioplasty or stent — excess morbidity and mortality

rules.condition: Progressing symptoms or recurrence despite DAPT, SBP <140 and high-intensity statin (medical failure)
rules.recommendation: Usefulness of angioplasty or stenting is unknown — neuro-IR discussion

evidenceNote: Kleindorfer 2021: COR 3: No Benefit, LOE B-R

options.doseText: Aspirin 325 mg daily + clopidogrel 75 mg daily up to 90 days, then aspirin alone
notes: Load clopidogrel if within the acute DAPT window
Agent details, interactions and holds: see the agent entries

institutionVaries: Neuro-IR thresholds for rescue angioplasty/stenting in medical failures
pearls: Warfarin vs aspirin (WASID): more major hemorrhage and death without fewer strokes

Rule 3 rests on a THALES prespecified subgroup: the analysis used ≥30% ipsilateral stenosis that didn't have to be related to the index event, both drugs were loaded, and bleeding was not significantly higher than with aspirin alone (Kleindorfer 2021 §5.1.1)
sources: Kleindorfer DO, et al. 2021 Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2021;52:e364-e467. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000375
